subject: Post-migration attribution gap — charged tokens don't match our telemetry
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmeai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@acmeai.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy after model migration — urgent ask

Hi Neha,

We're seeing a discrepancy between the token counts reported by our telemetry and the tokens billed on the Mar 1–14 billing window. After we migrated to the new v4-opt variant on Mar 1, our internal instrumentation shows ~2.8M tokens consumed, but your invoice and the usage export appear to show ~4.0M tokens — a ~1.2M delta charged to us.

We double-checked on our side: request IDs and session IDs line up with what we sent. Can you provide a per-request breakdown for 2028-03-01 00:00 UTC through 2028-03-14 23:59 UTC (request id, model variant, token in, token out, billing tenant) and any notes about routing changes during migration? This is blocking our AP team — they flagged the invoice for hold until we reconcile.

Please treat as high priority; if you need sample request_ids I can share 10 examples. Also: we operate under EU reverse-charge VAT; if there is a credit, we need it reflected with the correct VAT treatment.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform, Acme AI
alyssa.chen@acmeai.com
---
Attachment: sample-request-ids.txt (plain text)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy after model migration — urgent ask

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the note and sorry for the disruption.

Quick status: I've opened a ticket with billing and infra (cc'd Ben and David). Ben, can you pull the export and confirm if tokens were double-attributed or routed to a different tenant? David, please confirm whether the Mar 1 migration included any routing/variant aliasing that could explain cross-account attribution.

Alyssa — if you can share 10 of the sample request_ids (as you offered) that will speed things up. We'll aim to provide a per-request CSV and a proposed credit (if warranted) within 72 hours. If we need longer, we'll let you know and place a temporary hold on collection for the disputed amount.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Office: +1 415-555-0123
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2028 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy after model migration — urgent ask

Team — quick summary of what I found after an initial pull of the ingestion logs and billing attribution tables:

- Root observation: between 2028-03-01 00:00 UTC and 2028-03-02 06:00 UTC there was a brief window where our variant aliasing service forwarded traffic for an internal Acme test org to Acme's production tenant identifier. That caused ~1.18M tokens to be billed to their production account rather than the internal test org.

- Cause: during the v4-opt rollout we updated alias routing rules and one legacy alias (acme-internal-test) had a stale mapping to the production tenant. The routing change was reverted once discovered.

- Impact: ~1.18M tokens over 30 hours, primarily short-chat sessions with a mean length of 24 tokens. No other customers affected.

Attached: a sanitized export (usage-export-20280301-20280314.csv) with per-request billing_tenant and request_id columns; I redacted payloads.

Proposed remediation: issue a credit for the exact billed amount for the misattributed tokens (we calculate ~€1,420 gross). We'll produce a credit memo and apply it to Acme's account for the Mar invoice. Ben to coordinate with accounting for EU VAT reverse-charge handling.

Next actions:
- David: please confirm logs/timestamps and add a short postmortem blurb about guardrails to prevent alias staleness.
- Neha: I'll prepare the credit memo draft and share with Alyssa for signoff.

Ben Carter
Billing Operations Lead
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
---
Attachment: usage-export-20280301-20280314.csv (CSV, redacted)
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmeai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts@acmeai.com
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 08:09:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discrepancy after model migration — urgent ask

Thanks for the fast turnaround Ben — that matches what we suspected and the request_id samples you pulled match our internal logs.

Two asks before we close this:
1) Can you confirm the credit will be net of VAT and that the credit memo will be issued as a negative invoice reflecting EU reverse-charge (we'll need the document for our AP records)?
2) Will this appear on the corrected Mar invoice or as a separate credit applied to the next billing cycle? Our auditors prefer a separate credit memo so they can tie it to the original invoice.

If you can attach the credit memo draft and the accounting ticket (or HubSpot record) I can loop in our finance team to confirm.

Appreciate the remediation and the guardrail follow-up.

—Alyssa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, accounts@acmeai.com
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy after model migration — urgent ask

Hi Alyssa — confirmed:

- We've prepared a credit memo (credit-memo-ACME-20280318.pdf) for the gross billed amount of the misattributed tokens (~€1,420). The memo is issued as a negative line on its own document (not a reissued original invoice) so your AP/audit team can reconcile it against the Mar invoice.

- VAT handling: because Acme is an EU registered business using reverse-charge, accounting will record the credit memo with the reverse-charge tax code. I'll include a copy of the HubSpot record and the internal accounting ticket for traceability (HubSpot: 45829, JIRA: BILL-4821).

- Timeline: credit memo is posted today and will be applied as a credit on your next statement; if you prefer an immediate refund instead, we can handle that as well — please let me know which you prefer.

- Guardrails: David has scheduled a short postmortem and an automated alias-validation job to run during rollouts to prevent stale mappings.

I've attached the credit memo and the sanitized usage export we used for the calculation. Let me know if you need anything else.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Office: +1 415-555-0123
